title: Level 1 – Qualified Nurse
subtitle: Core Clinical Skills
intro: Welcome to GNPS Program 10 - Mastering Essential Clinical Skills. Core clinical skills form the foundation of safe nursing practice. Every procedure, from taking vital signs to wound care, requires preparation, patient identification, communication, infection prevention, technical accuracy and evaluation. This level is designed around the fundamental clinical capabilities expected within national nursing education programs and by nursing regulatory bodies across different countries. It develops the practical knowledge, procedural discipline and professional behaviours required to perform essential nursing interventions safely. Throughout this level you will strengthen your ability to: Prepare safely for clinical procedures Confirm identity, consent, allergies and relevant risks Measure and interpret vital signs accurately Apply standard precautions and aseptic principles Perform common clinical measurements and specimen collection Support safe medication administration Provide basic wound, catheter and device care Assist with mobility and manual handling Communicate, document and evaluate care A procedure can be technically correct but still unsafe if the wrong patient is treated, hand hygiene is missed, consent is not obtained or abnormal findings are ignored. Clinical competence includes both the skill and the judgement surrounding it. By the end of Level 1, you should be able to perform common nursing procedures safely and respectfully while following approved standards, organisational policy and your scope of practice. Level 1 - Qualified Nurse

content.text: Safe procedures begin before equipment is touched. The nurse should confirm the indication, assess the patient, explain the procedure, obtain consent, gather equipment and plan infection-prevention and safety measures.
Learning outcomes
Prepare a patient and environment for a clinical procedure Apply patient identification and consent requirements
Assess risks before beginning Maintain privacy, dignity and comfort

Patient Identification Use at least two approved identifiers before every procedure. Bed number, room location or familiarity is not sufficient. Any inconsistency should be resolved before proceeding.
Consent and Explanation Explain the purpose, key steps, expected sensations and possible discomfort in clear language. Confirm that the patient agrees and provide an opportunity for questions.
Pre-Procedure Assessment Review allergies, observations, pain, mobility, cognition, relevant results and contraindications. Consider whether assistance or escalation is needed.
Environment and Equipment Prepare a clean, private and well-lit space. Check that equipment is correct, intact, within expiry and functioning before use.

Before inserting a urinary catheter, the nurse confirms the patient's identity, explains the procedure, checks allergies, ensures privacy and prepares all equipment. When the patient reports a latex allergy, the standard kit is replaced before the procedure begins.
Key learning points
Safety begins before the procedure Use approved identifiers every time
Explain and obtain consent Check equipment, allergies and contraindications

Accurate measurement provides essential information about the patient's condition. Technique, interpretation and timely response are equally important. Recording a number without recognising its clinical meaning is incomplete nursing practice.
Learning outcomes
Measure vital signs accurately Perform focused respiratory, cardiovascular and neurological checks
Complete blood glucose, fluid balance and specimen-related tasks Recognise abnormal findings requiring escalation

Vital Signs and Pain Measure temperature, pulse, respirations, blood pressure, oxygen saturation and pain using correct equipment and technique. Compare results with the patient's baseline and recent trends.

Focused Assessment Respiratory assessment includes breathing pattern, effort, chest movement and breath sounds. Cardiovascular assessment includes pulse, perfusion, oedema and circulation. Neurological checks include consciousness, pupils, movement and relevant scoring tools.
Clinical Measurements Blood glucose monitoring, urinalysis, fluid balance and specimen collection require correct identification, preparation, technique and documentation.
Responding to Findings Repeat unexpected results when appropriate, assess the patient and escalate according to urgency. Do not delay action while waiting for a single severely abnormal value.

A patient appears drowsy and diaphoretic. Capillary blood glucose is low. The nurse confirms the result, assesses consciousness and swallowing safety, initiates the approved hypoglycaemia protocol and rechecks the response.
Key learning points
Use correct technique and functioning equipment Interpret findings in context
Look for trends and changes Act promptly on abnormal results

sections.title: Infection Prevention, Aseptic Technique and Device Care

content.text: Many clinical procedures create a pathway for microorganisms to enter vulnerable sites. Hand hygiene, appropriate PPE and protection of key parts and key sites are essential during wound, catheter, intravenous and enteral care.
Learning outcomes
Apply standard precautions during procedures Select and use PPE appropriately
Maintain an aseptic field Provide safe basic care for invasive devices
Hand Hygiene and PPE Perform hand hygiene at the appropriate moments and select PPE according to anticipated exposure. Gloves do not replace hand hygiene.
Aseptic Technique Prepare equipment, protect key parts and sites, avoid unnecessary contact and stop if contamination occurs. An unattended or compromised field should be re-established.
Wound Care Assess the wound, exudate, surrounding skin, pain and signs of infection. Use the ordered dressing and document findings objectively.
Device Care Catheters, peripheral intravenous lines and nasogastric tubes require securement, hygiene, patency checks, site assessment and review of ongoing need.

During wound care, the nurse accidentally touches a sterile key part with an unsterile glove. The contaminated item is discarded, hand hygiene is repeated and the field is re-established rather than continuing.
Key learning points
Protect key parts and key sites Treat suspected contamination as contamination
Assess devices and wounds, not only the dressing Remove unnecessary invasive devices promptly through approved processes
Clinical skills are integrated. Medication administration, mobility assistance, patient education and documentation all require safety checks, communication and evaluation.
Learning outcomes
Apply core medication administration principles Assist patients with mobility safely
Communicate throughout procedures Document care accurately and objectively
Medication Administration Confirm the order, patient, medicine, dose, route, time, allergies and relevant assessment. Prepare one patient's medicines at a time and monitor the response.
Mobility and Manual Handling Assess strength, balance, cognition and required assistance. Use approved equipment and techniques to protect both patient and staff.
Communication Explain each step, check comfort, invite questions and use therapeutic language. Patients should know how to report pain, dizziness or other concerns.
Documentation Record the assessment, procedure, findings, patient response and follow-up. Documentation should be timely, factual and completed after the intervention.

A patient becomes dizzy during transfer from bed to chair. The nurse stops, supports the patient safely, calls for assistance, checks observations and documents the event and response. Completing the transfer is not prioritised over safety.
Key learning points
Combine technical skill with ongoing assessment Stop when the patient's condition changes
Use safe manual-handling methods Document what was done and how the patient responded

End-of-Program Summary By completing GNPS Program 10 - Level 1, you have developed the foundational knowledge and practical behaviours required to prepare, perform, evaluate and document essential nursing procedures safely. These capabilities prepare you for Level 2 - International Qualified Nurse, where procedural skill is integrated with international standards, simulation and more complex clinical judgement.
